header: This builds the "Source" line under a health check-up answer: which circular(s) the rows were read from, and on which page each listed person stands, so that a click opens the circular in the viewer at that page. I do not ask the question-answering model for any of this (it would be one more thing for it to forget); the SYSTEM looks it up from what the answer returned: the circular label is a column of every check-up answer, and the page comes from the same view. Anything that goes wrong gives NO source line; the answer itself is never affected.

members.name: unconfirmed
doc: Names of the people in the answer that HR does not know (their ticket is shown as printed), in the order of the answer.

symbols.name: unconfirmedNote
symbols.sig: export function unconfirmedNote(unconfirmed: string[], listed: number): string | null
doc: Builds the sentence under the Source line for when someone listed is not confirmed against HR; returns null when everybody is.

symbols.name: pendingScheduleNote
symbols.sig: export async function pendingScheduleNote(run: RunQuery): Promise<string | null>
doc: I use this sentence when an answer is empty: health check-up schedules whose circular was uploaded but whose rows are NOT in the system (the upload could not finish reading them, see circular_ingest_log), so a person is told why instead of being left to wonder. Returns null when there are none, and when anything goes wrong (the log table may not exist yet).

symbols.name: ticketsAsked
symbols.sig: export function ticketsAsked(question: string, sql: string): string[]
doc: The ticket numbers a health check-up question is about: the ones the SQL that ran filters on (ticket_no = '228757', or an IN list), and, when the SQL has none, I take six-digit numbers from the question itself. At most three.

symbols.name: scheduleAsked
symbols.sig: export function scheduleAsked(sql: string): string | null
doc: The schedule a question asked about, named the way the schedules are named ("January 2025") and read from the SQL that ran; returns null when the SQL does not name one.

symbols.name: ticketLookupNote
symbols.sig: export async function ticketLookupNote(run: RunQuery, tickets: string[], askedLabel: string | null = null): Promise<string | null>
doc: I use this for an EMPTY health check-up answer about a ticket, so that it is said the way a person would say it. What was asked comes first ("Ticket 228757 is not on the January 2025 health check-up list."), then who the ticket belongs to (the HR directory) and every list it IS on, so an empty answer is never a dead end. Returns null when there is nothing to say or anything goes wrong (the reason is written to the server log; the answer then stays as it was).

symbols.name: emptyScheduleAnswer
symbols.sig: export function emptyScheduleAnswer(args: { person: string | null; askedLabel: string | null; have: string[] }): string

params.name: args
params.type: { person: string | null; askedLabel: string | null; have: string[] }

doc: The whole text of an EMPTY health check-up answer. `person` is the ticket sentence (or null), `askedLabel` the schedule the question named (or null), `have` the schedules that exist. I give the list of schedules only when it helps: when the month asked about does not exist, or when nothing else can be said.

behaviours: one circular: one source with its id, label, full title and the pages of the listed people (3 and 4), not the page of someone not in the answer (7)
a person on two schedules: one source per circular, in the order the answer shows them (December first here), each with its own page
many rows of one circular give ONE source line (not one per row)
a row with no ticket is placed by name (page 5)
an answer without a 'circular' column gets no source line and no lookup is made
no rows: nothing
rows whose circular is empty: nothing
a failing lookup gives NO source line (and no error): the answer itself is unaffected
a circular whose id cannot be found has no link (never a link without an id)
pages unknown: the source line is still given (the viewer opens at the first page)
a circular id that is not a whole number is never used
a page that is not a positive whole number is ignored
both lookups read only nlq.health_checkups, and the values travel as parameters (nothing from the answer is pasted into the SQL)
people HR does not know are named, in the order of the answer (found by ticket, or by name when there is no ticket)
when everybody is confirmed there is nobody to name
someone unconfirmed who is NOT in the answer (100099) is never named
a row with no 'verified' value is not called unconfirmed (only an explicit false is)
the note: nobody -> none
the note: one person looked up -> 'This person is not in the HR directory ...' (no counts)
the note: one of a list -> '1 of the 15 people listed is not ...' (singular verb) with the name
the note: several -> plural verb, all names
the note: more than five names -> five and 'and N more' (the line stays short)
nothing pending: no sentence
one schedule not read yet: named by its archive label
two: 'A and B', plural
three: 'A, B and C'
a circular with no serial number is named by its headline
if the log table does not exist yet: no sentence, no error
the ticket is read from the SQL that ran: ticket_no = '228757'
...also an IN list, and two tickets are both kept
with no ticket in the SQL, a six-digit number in the question is used; a number of another length is not
the SQL wins over the question, and at most three tickets are kept
no ticket anywhere: nothing
the schedule asked about is read from the SQL: year 2025, month 1 -> 'January 2025'
...a month of 12 -> December; a schedule named in words is used as written
a SQL that names no schedule, only a year, or an impossible month gives null
the 12 Oct case, in plain words: what was asked first, then who he is and where he IS
...it never says 'row' or 'no row matches' (database language), and has no doubled brackets '))' in a row of nested text
on two lists: both are named, in order, and the question's own list is the one said to be missing from
a ticket HR knows that is on no list
HR's department may be missing: the name alone is given
a ticket on a list that HR does not know (a person who has left)
a ticket nobody knows
when the question named no list the sentence says 'that health check-up list'
two tickets: one paragraph each
if the lookup fails: nothing is added, no error (the answer stays as it was)
no tickets: nothing
about a ticket, the list asked about exists: just the person sentence (no list of schedules, which has nothing to do with the question)
about a ticket, the list asked about does NOT exist: the sentence, then that there is no such list and which lists there are
not about a ticket: 'Nothing was found.' and the lists that exist
...and when it asked for a list that does not exist, it says so first
no list loaded at all
no jargon anywhere in these answers ('row', 'no row matches')
